SaftyPLC.no_data: No Safety PLC data (waiting for push)
SaftyPLC.help_overview_p1: This table shows live Result signals from the SICK Flexi Compact (FLX3-CPUC200) Safety PLC over Modbus TCP. The vehicle controller maps each bit via SaftyPLCMap.json to semantic signals (EMO, Bumper, Lidar, Bypass, etc.) and pushes updates here through SignalR.
SaftyPLC.help_overview_p2: The table shows both the hardware raw bit and the logic state after polarity is applied. Alarms and speed control use the logic state, not the raw bit directly.
SaftyPLC.help_status_conn: Whether communication with the Safety PLC is active and status is being received.
SaftyPLC.help_status_sim: Local simulator mode is active. Raw values can be clicked when connected, in simulator mode, and logged in with permission.
SaftyPLC.help_status_device: Device status string reported by the Safety PLC (e.g. normal operation / fault).
SaftyPLC.help_status_updated: Timestamp of the latest status push.
SaftyPLC.help_col_address: Two address layers. Top B{byte}.{bit} is the Safety Designer Input Data Block byte/bit (e.g. B6.0). Bottom IR{reg}.{bit} is the Modbus Input Register address and bit-in-word after big-endian conversion. Use these when debugging wiring or communication.
SaftyPLC.help_col_signal: Fixed semantic signal name used by software (enum string), e.g. XTDO1_Q2_EMO_Status or CPUC200_I15_Front_Lidar_Bypass. The polarity API also identifies signals by this name.
SaftyPLC.help_col_description: Human-readable text from SaftyPLCMap.json for operators. It does not affect control logic.
SaftyPLC.help_col_raw: Raw Modbus bit (0 or 1) before polarity. Row background follows Raw=1 (green) / Raw=0 (white). Clickable only when connected in simulator mode and logged in with permission, to inject simulated inputs.
SaftyPLC.help_col_logic: Logic state after polarity: ON or OFF. This is what vehicle control uses. Example: ActiveHigh with Raw=1 → ON; ActiveLow with Raw=0 → ON. Hover to see the Raw→Logic hint.
SaftyPLC.help_col_polarity: Polarity setting. A-High (ActiveHigh): Raw=1 means logic ON. A-Low (ActiveLow): Raw=0 means logic ON (common for NC / B-contacts). Logged-in users can click to toggle; the change is saved to SaftyPLCMap.json and logic is recomputed immediately.
SaftyPLC.help_relation_title: How Raw, Logic, and Polarity relate
SaftyPLC.help_relation_high: A-High: Raw 1→ON, Raw 0→OFF. Typical XTDO safety status is Raw=1 when normal and Raw=0 when tripped; keep A-High so a trip becomes logic OFF.
SaftyPLC.help_relation_low: A-Low: Raw 0→ON, Raw 1→OFF. Use only when contact polarity is inverted from the above.
SaftyPLC.help_relation_p2: Wrong polarity inverts alarms and speed control (normal looks abnormal and vice versa). Confirm electrical design and Safety Designer routing before changing.
SaftyPLC.help_usage_search: The search box filters by Signal, Description, address (B / IR), Raw, ON/OFF, A-High/A-Low, etc. The counter shows matched / total rows.
SaftyPLC.help_usage_raw: In simulator mode after login, click Raw → confirm → backend writes the simulated bit and pushes an update. Without login, or on production (non-simulator), Raw cannot be changed.
SaftyPLC.help_usage_polarity: After login, click Polarity → confirm → map file is updated and status is pushed. Without login, polarity is read-only.
SaftyPLC.help_usage_row_color: Row background follows Raw (1=light green, 0=white). Treat this separately from the Logic ON/OFF text color.
SaftyPLC.help_tips_xtdo: For typical XTDO1_Q1~Q8 safety outputs, normal=Raw 1 and tripped=Raw 0. Keep A-High. Vehicle control treats logic OFF as abnormal and raises the matching alarm.
SaftyPLC.help_tips_persist: Polarity changes persist in SaftyPLCMap.json (usually /home/gpm/param/SaftyPLCMap.json in production; Debug may write Documents/param). Settings survive restart.
SaftyPLC.help_tips_logic_alarm: Alarms and laser decelerate/stop logic all use logic state. When troubleshooting, compare Raw and Polarity together to verify Logic matches the field.
